newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania left snubs president's offer of clemency.
newsitem.headline: Albania left snubs president's offer of clemency.

text.p: Albania's opposition Socialist Party on Monday rejected an offer by conservative President Sali Berisha to cut the jail term of Socialist leader Fatos Nano by six months.
Berisha issued a decree on Sunday pardoning or reducing the jail sentences of 102 prisoners.
"If he is not going to free him (Nano)...then he may as well not cut his sentence by six months," said senior Socialist Namik Dokle.
Nano, 43, was jailed for 12 years in 1994 on charges of embezzlement during his brief stint as prime minister in 1991 but Socialists argue he is being held as a political prisoner.
His jail term has been cut on previous occasions and he has about 16 months of his sentence left to serve.
International rights groups, which have raised doubts over the legality of Nano's trial, have called for his release but Berisha has resisted the pressure.
Dokle said even if Berisha freed Nano from the remote high-security Benca jail in southern Albania, he would still want to be declared innocent of the charges on which he was convicted.
"It is clear again that Nano frightens Berisha because presidential elections are ahead and he does not want Nano to be free when they are held," Dokle said.
Socialists boycotted a controversial general election in May, accusing Berisha's Democratic Party of rigging the poll. They refuse to take up the handful of seats they were allotted in parliament.
